Unconscionable consideration under the Indian Claims Commission Act requires a very gross disparity between price and value, judged on all the facts and circumstances and not by a mechanical percentage formula.
fixes.now: Under the Indian Claims Commission Act, disparity in price alone establishes unconscionable consideration only where there is a very gross inequality, judged on each case's facts and circumstances and not by a mechanical percentage formula.

fixes.was: A mandatory employment arbitration agreement is enforceable for statutory discrimination claims only if it preserves the employee's unwaivable statutory rights, and it is unconscionable if it requires arbitration of the employee's claims but not the employer's without justification.
fixes.now: A mandatory employment arbitration agreement may cover FEHA claims only if it preserves the employee's unwaivable statutory rights, and an adhesive agreement is unconscionable if it requires arbitration of the employee's claims but not the employer's corresponding claims without a reasonable business justification.

fixes.now: affirmed the order denying Empire's request to stay the action and compel arbitration.
